description: In Quantitative Aptitude, the Average represents the central value of a given set of data. It is fundamentally calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations, providing a quick summary metric for data interpretation and comparison.

sections.title: Basic Concept
sections.description: Fundamental understanding of averages and the primary formula used for calculation.

equations: Average = Sum of all observations / Total number of observations
Sum of observations = Average * Total number of observations

sections.title: Properties of Averages
sections.description: The effect of basic mathematical operations applied uniformly to all numbers in a dataset.

cases.condition: If a constant 'x' is added to or subtracted from each observation in a dataset.
If each observation is multiplied or divided by a non-zero constant 'x'.

sections.title: Averages of Number Series
sections.description: Direct formulas to quickly calculate the averages of standard arithmetic progressions and number series.

equations: Average of first 'n' odd numbers = n
Average of consecutive numbers (or any Arithmetic Progression) = (First Term + Last Term) / 2

sections.title: Weighted Average
sections.description: Calculating the combined average when different groups with different individual averages are merged.

key_concepts.explanation: If Group 1 has 'n1' items with an average of 'A1', and Group 2 has 'n2' items with an average of 'A2', the combined average of both groups is calculated as (n1 * A1 + n2 * A2) / (n1 + n2). This logic extends to any number of merging groups.

sections.title: Deviation Method
sections.description: An advanced, time-saving technique to find the average of large, closely grouped numbers without heavy calculations.

steps.title: Choose Assumed Average
steps.detail: Select an assumed average (A) that is visually close to the given numbers to simplify calculations.

steps.title: Find Individual Deviations
steps.detail: Calculate the difference of each number from the assumed average (Deviation = Given Number - A).

steps.title: Calculate Net Deviation
steps.detail: Sum all the individual deviations together, carefully accounting for positive and negative signs.

steps.title: Determine Final Average
steps.detail: Apply the final formula: Final Average = Assumed Average (A) + (Net Deviation / Total number of observations).

sections.title: Inclusion, Exclusion, and Replacement
sections.description: Rules for solving scenarios where members join, leave, or are swapped within a group.

cases.condition: When a new member joins the group (Inclusion).
results: Value of New Member = Old Average + (New Total Members * Increase in Average)

cases.condition: When an existing member leaves the group (Exclusion).
results: Value of Leaving Member = Old Average - (Remaining Members * Increase in Average)

cases.condition: When an existing member is replaced by a new member (Replacement).
results: Value of New Member = Value of Replaced Member + (Total Members * Increase in Average)
